focus.title: Beaded plant Suncatcher
focus.summary: Sunlight has a way of bringing a space to life. As it passes through a window, it fills a room with color, movement, and small moments that make a house feel like home. In this workshop, participants create beaded plant sun catchers inspired by the light that streams through our windows and the natural elements we welcome into our homes. By combining colorful beads and delicate forms, each piece is designed to catch and reflect sunlight, creating shifting patterns of color and light. The result is a decorative artwork that celebrates the warmth of home through nature, color, and light.
focus.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Echoes of the Familiar
queue.summary: Echoes of the Familiar exhibition explores the concept that home transcends mere physical space, embodying a tapestry of memories intricately woven into its very walls. It is within these confines that the echoes of laughter from childhood games intermingle with the remnants of disagreements and tears shed upon pillows. Each drawer brims with knick-knacks whose purposes remain elusive yet evoke nostalgia. The scent of maternal cooking and the rhythmic snoring of a father create a comforting ambiance, while the presence of a grandmother before the television grounds us in familial continuity. These shared experiences resonate universally, forging a collective nostalgia for "al zaman al Jameel

queue.title: Tafasahu: Make Room
queue.summary: Tafasahu: Make Room is an exhibition that showcases a commissioned installation by Saudi architect and artist, Nada AlMulla, which invites you to enter as a guest—to pause, gather and reflect on the conditions of belonging within the context of the traditional Majlis, Arabic for "gathering space." Beyond being a place to receive and host guests, the Majlis has been a vessel for the transmission of knowledge and heritage. The installation deconstructs this space into its essential elements while centering stories, memories and subtle traces of everyday life that animated it: conversations shared over coffee, the lingering scent of incense, the rhythms of gathering and departure. queue.title: Ajeeb in Wonder House
queue.summary: A story-led experience that follows Ajeeb as he visits a series of unusual homes, each shaped by a different idea, form, or function. As the story unfolds, children observe how each space reflects a way of living, then shift into designing a home that suits Ajeeb himself. The activity combines storytelling with creative decision-making, moving from observation to design.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: 1, 2, 3, A Little Space for Me
queue.summary: Small spaces can hold big discoveries. Designed for children under three with their parents, this environment is divided into three distinct zones: movement, hands-on exploration, and quiet play. Each area offers a different way to engage, from active motion to focused interaction and calm building. The experience supports early development through movement, touch, and shared exploration.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: 1, 2, 3, Let's Rhyme!
queue.summary: Come sing along with us as we explore beloved nursery rhymes, discover new ones, and enjoy a wonderful storytelling experience. Connect with other families in a welcoming environment that promotes early childhood development and provides lots of entertainment. This session, lasting for 30 minutes, is ideal for children aged 0 to 3 years.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: A Home I Imagine
queue.summary: A home can begin as an idea and take shape in many forms. In this workshop, imagination leads the design process. Through drawing, building, and assembling materials, children develop their own vision of a home and translate it into a tangible model. Each creation results in a constructed home that reflects personal ideas and vision.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Around the Table
queue.summary: An interactive activity where children explore how dining tables bring together different cultural practices. The program introduces a range of customs and habits from around the world, showing how the way people gather, sit, and share meals can differ from one place to another. Through simple role-play, children take part in everyday moments such as greeting others, welcoming guests, and spending time around a table.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Built by Nature
queue.summary: A bird’s nest, a termite mound, a shell, each one is carefully built, not by chance, but by need. In this workshop, children observe how living things design their homes, then borrow these ideas to sketch and shape their own. Openings for air, layers for protection, and smart use of materials begin to appear in their designs. What starts in nature slowly turns into a built form.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Children's Café
queue.summary: Step into the Children’s Café, a truly unique experience created just for your child! A space where little ones can enjoy their very own café moment, designed at their scale, where they choose, create and explore freely. From decorating their treats at the Art Toppings Station to relaxing in a cozy Reading Corner, every detail is made to spark joy and imagination. It’s more than a café... it’s a first-of-its-kind experience where children gain confidence in their creativity.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Draw Your Story
queue.summary: Drawing is one way to represent spaces, ideas, and everyday life to tell their stories through them. In this open drawing space, children use different materials to create images related to their home, activities, and surroundings.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Hidden Home Bingo
queue.summary: A simple object at home might have a story that starts far beyond the room it sits in. In this fast-paced bingo challenge, children move through clues and questions, connecting everyday items to the materials behind them. As matches come together, unexpected links appearو turning familiar spaces into something to decode and discover.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Insightful Spaces
queue.summary: The way we experience a space is shaped by what we feel under our feet, not just what we see. In this sensory journey, children touch different carpeted surfaces, noticing textures, patterns, and subtle changes in sensation. As they explore, they begin to recognize how materials influence comfort, sound and perception in everyday spaces.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Interactive Exhibit
queue.summary: An open-ended interactive exhibition that invites children to explore, create, and play through hands-on experiences. It encourages curiosity, imagination, and discovery for children and their families.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Let’s Decorate!
queue.summary: Decorations change depending on the occasion, the place, and the people. At the Inspiration Spot, children get inspired to make different styles to celebrate.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Mic Moments
queue.summary: Everyday life is full of small details, routines, habits, and traditions that differ from one home to another. In this street mic–style activity, children respond to short, guided questions about their daily life. The format is open and conversational, allowing them to speak, listen, and hear different perspectives in a simple setup.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Mirror Or Window
queue.summary: Some images reflect what we already know, others reveal something new. In this interactive experience, artworks are explored as shifting viewpoints. Certain scenes echo familiar memories, while others introduce different ways of living and seeing the world. Through guided observation and creative response, children interpret what they see and translate it into visual expression. The experience results in personal interpretations shaped by both recognition and discovery.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: My Family Bouquet
queue.summary: A bouquet grows, one flower at a time. In this hands-on workshop, children begin with simple shapes and watch them take form as each piece is rolled, combined, and built into a flower. Colors are chosen, details are added, and the process repeats, each new bloom adding to the whole. As the bouquet comes together, each flower stands for someone at home, gathered into one arrangement shaped through making and choice.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Our Place on Earth
queue.summary: A house in the desert is not built like one by the sea, and for good reason. In this experience, children explore how homes respond to their environments, from heat to movement to moisture. This leads into building and testing simple structures, adjusting them to stand against different conditions.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Painted Faces
queue.summary: What's a festival without facepainting? Children choose from a variety of designs and have them painted using safe, child-friendly colors.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Treasures in Every Home
queue.summary: Deep within the Earth, metal begins its journey, formed over time and transformed into materials we use every day at home. In this interactive workshop, children follow this journey, then reshape a simple tin container into a new functional object. The activity introduces how materials can be reused and redesigned for new purposes..
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Where We Belong
queue.summary: Look closely at Earth, and it begins to feel like a system that never stops working; air moving, water cycling, living things adapting. In this program, children explore how life continues and changes across different environments, and how organisms adjust to survive over time. The journey then stretches further, looking at how science studies these systems and reimagines them beyond Earth. The experience connects life, environment, and possibility in one continuous story.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Who Lived Here?
queue.summary: Every landscape shapes the homes built within it. This treasure hunt in Rehlaat Gallery, children follow clues across three environments: desert, mountain, and coast. Each stop reveals a model home designed in response to its surroundings, from materials and structure to layout and function. As they move between locations, children match clues to the correct homes, discovering how climate, terrain, and daily life influence the way people build and live.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: Zoom In
queue.summary: A tiny fragment holds the clue. In this Praise of the Artisan treasure hunt, children begin with a zoomed-in detail taken from a larger artwork, a pattern, texture, or small visual hint. Moving through the space, they search for the full piece, matching what they see up close with what appears on the walls. As the search unfolds, attention shifts to details that are often overlooked, building observation skills through careful looking. Each match reveals the complete artwork behind the fragment.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: In the Home of…
queue.summary: Some homes are easy to recognize. Others leave clues behind. In this interactive library experience, children move through a series of spaces, each one arranged as a “home” shaped by a well-known literary character. Objects, layouts, and small details hint at who might live there. As they explore each corner, children follow prompts and challenges that guide them to observe, connect, and identify the character behind each space. The experience unfolds step by step, turning the library into a trail of clues where stories are discovered through place, detail, and interaction.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: My Little Fort
queue.summary: Many children create small spaces of their own at home—under a table, behind cushions, or inside a blanket fort. In this hands-on activity, children build their own small “fort” using soft materials, shaping a space they can define and arrange. The session ends with a short story connected to the idea of shared spaces and home.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: My Neighbor Totoro
queue.summary: A gentle and magical tale by Studio Ghibli that celebrates the innocence of childhood, the quiet beauty of nature, and the meaning of home found in family. Through the eyes of two sisters who move to the countryside, the story unfolds into a world of forest spirits and unseen friends.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

queue.title: On This Carpet
queue.summary: in Echoes of the Familiar Gallery, around every corner, a story unfolds. This workshop takes place on a carpet filled with familiar scenes, where everyday moments take shape through storytelling and creative exploration. Children move through these scenes, connecting details, building narratives, and expressing their ideas through drawing and simple story-making. Each visit brings together small moments into a larger picture, shaped by observation, memory, and imagination.
queue.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra

A set of outdoor water-based activities where children move between water games that include pouring, splashing, and balancing tasks.

queue.title: The House of Ideas
queue.summary: We begin with a simple question: Where do ideas live? Like us, ideas need a place where they feel safe in a space that inspires them and gives them room to grow. In this experience, we explore the House of Ideas: where we will see how a thought begins, what nurtures it and how we can create spaces that allow it to flourish. By designing a pop-up house inside a notebook, participants build a small, personal world where their ideas can live and take shape. Through cutting, folding and creating, a quiet reflection unfolds: what helps our ideas grow, and where do they truly belong

queue.title: Unbox Your Story
queue.summary: What if we combine reality with fantasy? How would that enrich your story? Join us for a fun family experience as you discover a new world of stories full with boundless imagination and possibilities. All you have to do is open the box in front of you to reveal the tools and materials within. Begin creating your characters and designing your plot with the various elements available to you. Unleash your creativity and share your new story with those around you!

queue.summary: In a world filled with imagination and wonder, niMú embarks on an unexpected journey among suitcases, dreams, and ordinary moments that transform into extraordinary stories. queue.summary: What begins on a screen doesn’t have to stay there. In this experience, children explore a virtual space, then follow clear steps to bring part of it into the real world. Piece by piece, what was seen on screen becomes something they can build and hold in reality.

queue.title: Art Futures Camp 2026 – Diriyah Art Futures
queue.summary: Art Futures Summer Camp for Arabic-Speaking Teens is a three-week immersive programme hosted by Diriyah Art Futures (DAF), the MENA region’s first centre dedicated to New Media Arts. Designed for Arabic-speaking teens aged 14–18, the camp offers an in-depth introduction to digital art practices in a dynamic and supportive environment. Under the 2026 theme, “Digital Art and Portraiture,” participants explore new ways of representing identity in the digital age, questioning how individuals are portrayed when faces become data and images circulate beyond physical presence. The programme combines creative experimentation with foundational technical skills, including Fab Lab practices and digital studio portraiture. Throughout the camp, participants work closely with industry specialists and creative mentors, culminating in a collaborative exhibition produced with DAF’s curatorial and exhibition teams to showcase their work. Applications are officially open, with aspiring young creatives in Riyadh able to apply until Sunday, June 7.

queue.title: Horses and Equestrian Heritage Exhibition
queue.summary: The King Abdulaziz Public Library is hosting a specialized exhibition on horses and equestrian heritage in celebration of Saudi Founding Day. The exhibition showcases a rich collection of manuscripts, rare books, photographs, historical documents, Islamic miniatures, and illustrated works highlighting the deep-rooted equestrian legacy of the Kingdom. Marking four decades of preserving cultural heritage, the library also presents selections from its dedicated Equestrian Center, which houses more than 12,000 rare Arabic and international references on horses, alongside historic photographs captured by Princess Alice of Britain during her 1938 visit to Saudi Arabia.

queue.summary: The Saudi Food Show returns to Riyadh Front Exhibition & Convention Center, bringing together global food and beverage leaders to showcase the latest trends, products, and innovations shaping the Kingdom’s fast-growing F&B sector. Alongside the exhibition floor, the Elite Lounge serves as the heart of the Tawasul Meetings—a premium space where top buyers meet top brands and conversations turn into real business impact. queue.title: Saudi International Falcons & Hunting Exhibition
queue.summary: The Saudi International Falcons and Hunting Exhibition is one of the largest events dedicated to falconry and hunting in Saudi and globally. It brings together everything related to falconry and outdoor excursions, from falcons and hunting tools to equipment and gear associated with hunting trips, all within a comprehensive space that allows visitors to explore this field in one place. The exhibition also features platforms showcasing a wide range of brands, alongside accompanying activities and events suitable for families, creating an experience that blends cultural and entertainment elements. The event plays an important role in preserving falconry heritage and raising awareness by offering content that introduces visitors to its history and significance within Saudi’s cultural identity.

queue.title: Saudi Falcons Club Auction
queue.summary: The Saudi Falcons Club organizes an annual auction dedicated to locally caught falcons, known as “Al Tarh falcons,” which are captured during the hunting season. The auction is a structured platform that brings falconers together to showcase their falcons in a competitive live bidding environment, enabling reliable buying and selling. The event is broadcast on television channels and digital platforms. The club also provides integrated services for falcon owners, including transportation to the auction venue, along with facilities that organize and enhance the participation experience, all within a framework aimed at developing falcon auctions in Saudi. The auction also contributes to raising awareness about preserving falcon breeds by regulating sales and emphasizing the protection of endangered species.
